items.title: PCRS and NHS Wales primary care respiratory update, Cardiff, 20 October 2026
items.summary: PCRS is running a one-day essential primary care respiratory update in Cardiff on Tuesday 20 October 2026, with NHS Wales Performance and Improvement and members of the National Respiratory Audit Programme. A concentrated Welsh primary care respiratory audience.

items.title: Inability to book GP appointments online is causing ‘a lot of frustration’, says NHSE chair
items.summary: There is ‘a lot of frustration’ from patients about not being able to book a GP appointment online and NHS England must accelerate work around this, the commissioner’s chair has said.

items.title: Nurses alerted to ‘potentially harmful’ online ads for baby products
items.summary: Nurses have been urged to be aware of ‘potentially harmful claims’ being made in online advertisements promoting certain baby products.

items.title: Vomiting in infants: when is it reflux, and when should we worry?
items.summary: Dilemmas in paediatrics: GPwER in paediatrics Dr David Capehorn discusses how to assess the vomiting infant, and distinguish normal physiology, overfeeding and milk allergy from the rare scenarios where a child needs urgent referral Note cases discussed in this article are hypothetical and created for educational…

items.title: PCOS to PMOS name change among featured sessions at free Pulse virtual event
items.summary: GPs are invited to a free two-day virtual event in October, focussed on everyday presentations in primary care.

items.title: Health news watch: the male contraceptive pill, assisted dying bill and more
items.summary: Here, we look at the clinical news that patients might have read in the mainstream news media in September and provide the original evidence behind the stories so that you can answer any questions that may come up. Cahal McQuillan reports.

items.title: Cervical screening updates and breast cancer prevention to feature at Nursing in Practice North
items.summary: Updates to the cervical screening programme – including the rollout of HPV self-testing kits – and a focus on breast cancer prevention and early detection will feature at our Nursing in Practice North 2026 event next month.

items.title: Guideline on diabetes distress calls for routine emotional checks
items.summary: Healthcare professionals should routinely discuss the emotional impact of diabetes with patients, according to a clinical practice guideline developed by the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD).

items.title: Clinical quiz: managing UTI in women
items.summary: Women frequently present with symptoms of urinary tract infection (UTI) in primary care, but diagnosis and treatment are not always straightforward. Nurses need to recognise when symptoms support an empirical diagnosis, when urine testing is useful and when red flags suggest pyelonephritis or another cause.

items.title: Expanded health visiting support to be rolled out across 1,000 family hubs
items.summary: The government has announced plans to expand health visiting and midwifery support in family hubs across all local authorities by 2028.

items.title: GP reimbursement scheme expanded to locums and funding transfers
items.summary: The GP practice-level reimbursement scheme has been expanded today to include self-employed locums, and to allow practices to transfer any unused funding to any other practice.

items.title: MenB vaccination only taken up by a quarter of students heading for university
items.summary: Three-quarters of Year 13 students eligible for the meningitis B vaccine have not taken up the offer available through pharmacies, public health officials warn.

items.title: Infant feeding and mental health support to be rolled out across England by 2028
items.summary: A ‘Healthy Babies’ programme like what used to be provided in Sure Start centres will be rolled out to all local authorities by 2028, the Government has announced.

items.title: NMC fee increase comes into force
items.summary: An almost 20% increase to the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) registration fee comes into force from today (1 October). In a statement for Nursing in Practice, the NMC has set out what nurses, midwives and nursing associates can expect when it comes to their payments following the increase.

items.title: GPs to refer to new specialist services for domestic abuse support in 12 ICBs
items.summary: GPs will be able to refer people to ‘new specialist services’ for domestic abuse support in 12 ICB areas, the Government has announced. At the Labour Party Conference in Liverpool today, health secretary Yvette Cooper announced the rollout of the services would be backed by almost £50m.

items.title: NHS England’s GP list-cleansing drive targeting six to seven million patients
items.summary: Exclusive NHS England’s current GP list-cleansing drive is targeting six to seven million patients, new documents have revealed.

items.title: Government to create national pension scheme for social care nurses
items.summary: A new national pension scheme is to be created for nurses and colleagues working in the social care sector, the government has announced.

items.title: ‘How GPs are using AI as a clinical reasoning tool – rather than just a search function’
items.summary: Dr Kevin Fernando contemplates how GPs’ use of AI is changing in clinical practice, evaluating results from a query analysis carried out by Medscape Artificial intelligence (AI) is already changing the way we find information in our daily lives, but how are GPs really using it in clinical consultations?

items.title: Public more likely to trust health advice from GPs than any other source, survey finds
items.summary: The public are more likely to trust information and health advice from their GP than any other source, a new survey commissioned by the RCGP has found.

items.title: GPs call for ‘parachute payments’ as list cleansing puts practices at risk of ‘going under’
items.summary: GP leaders across London have asked for urgent ‘parachute payments’ for practices facing sudden income loss from NHS England’s ongoing aggressive list-cleansing exercise.

items.title: Moving vaccinations out of practices ‘frees up nurse time but adds workload complexity’
items.summary: Moving vaccinations out of Scottish GP practices has freed up nursing time but has increased the complexity of the profession’s workload, an analysis has found.

items.title: PCRS webinar on breathlessness and chronic cough in adults, 30 September
items.summary: PCRS emailed members on 14 August 2026 announcing a webinar, Breathlessness and chronic cough in adults: challenges currently being faced by primary care, on Wednesday 30 September 2026, 19:00 to 20:00. Date and time taken from the PCRS mailing; not yet confirmed on the public PCRS events listing.

items.title: Prime Minister issues apology to social care nurses for ‘being let down for so long’
items.summary: The Prime Minister has assured nurses and other professionals working in social care they are ‘not invisible’ to his government and has apologised for the way in which they have been ‘let down’ by politicians.

items.title: Proposed national care service ‘utterly essential’ to securing NHS future, says Burnham
items.summary: The Prime Minister has used his speech at the Labour Party conference to warn that a broken social care ‘will break the NHS too’.

items.title: ‘I’m not an anxious person, but general practice has pushed me to my limits’
items.summary: Dr Katie Musgrave opens up about the work-induced anxiety she has experienced in general practice, wondering if others are suffering in silence Has anybody else ever experienced that heart-sinking feeling when you’re due to go back to work after a holiday, and you just can’t face it?

items.title: ‘I wasn’t emotionally prepared for retiring from being a GP’
items.summary: Former GP Mary Coyne shares her experience of how the emotional impact of retiring caught her by surprise As I started to approach retirement, I began to wonder what it might look like. The standard definition of ‘leaving your job and stopping work’ was not to my liking.

items.title: GLP-1s and SGLT-2s may help slow kidney damage in diabetes, study shows
items.summary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor drugs slow decline in kidney function in people with type 2 diabetes, but the benefits are only seen if they also have albuminuria, a large US ‘real-world’ study has reported.

items.title: BMA opposes Government plans for trusts to commission primary care
items.summary: The BMA has opposed plans for trusts to commission primary care as part of the neighbourhood health model.

items.title: New ‘workplace health system’ to prevent GP fit notes
items.summary: The Government is pushing ahead with its plan to create a ‘workplace health system’ to help people stay in work and prevent the need for GP fit notes.

items.title: NMC four-year midwifery strategy targets racism and safety
items.summary: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) has set out a four-year strategy for midwifery regulation aimed at supporting safer maternity care, with equity and anti-racism among its listed priorities.

items.title: RCN president warns immigration reforms could destabilise social care
items.summary: Royal College of Nursing (RCN) president Bejoy Sebastian has renewed calls for the home secretary to scrap proposed immigration reforms for care workers, arguing they are incompatible with ambitions for a national care service and could further destabilise social care.

items.title: AP concerns ‘similar’ to those around physician associates, says BMA
items.summary: The BMA has demanded an ‘urgent review’ is launched by the Government into the scopes of practice for advanced practitioners.

items.title: Nurses caught ‘snooping’ on patient records will be suspended immediately, warns NHSE
items.summary: Nurses and health professionals suspected of accessing patient records ‘improperly and unlawfully’ will be suspended immediately, NHS England (NHSE) has warned.

items.title: Health visitors win job evaluation after industrial action
items.summary: Health visitors employed by NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde (NHS GCC) have halted industrial action after the health board agreed to complete a job evaluation process.

items.title: PM pledges to put NHS-style care service plans before electorate
items.summary: Plans for an NHS-style national care service, free at the point of delivery, will be in the Labour manifesto ahead of the next general election, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged. In a BBC interview, Mr Burnham warned that ‘broken social care will break the National Health Service if we leave it like it is’...

items.title: ‘When GPs think they know the whole story’
items.summary: Runner-up in our writing competition, Dr LM explores the danger of believing that GPs can understand a patient’s life from a single consultation, and the assumptions that quietly fill in the gaps The lie I tell my patients is that I understand. I nod at the right moments.

items.title: Persistent ketoacidosis risk found with SGLT2 diabetes drugs
items.summary: Patients taking widely used SGLT2 inhibitor drugs for type 2 diabetes can remain at risk of ketoacidosis throughout treatment, a large Scandinavian study suggests. Ketoacidosis is a potentially life-threatening complication caused by a build-up of ketones in the blood.

items.title: NHS England instructs GP practices to dismiss staff caught ‘snooping’ on patient records
items.summary: GP practices should sack employees caught ‘snooping’ patient records ‘in almost all cases’, according to NHS England.

items.title: Implementing Benedict’s law: guidance from a school nurse
items.summary: Following the launch of new statutory allergy safety guidance this month, all state-maintained schools, academies and free schools are expected to meet a number of requirements relating to staff allergy training and allergy safety policies, among other things.

items.title: A quicker way to work through patient symptoms
items.summary: Tiredness. Calf pain. A persistent cough. An unfamiliar rash. In primary care, a seemingly straightforward symptom can have a long list of possible causes. Nursing in Practice Reference is designed to help nurses work through them.

items.title: Semaglutide linked to 40% reduction in asthma attacks
items.summary: Weight loss and diabetes treatment semaglutide is associated with a nearly 40% reduction in asthma attacks among people with the condition, according to new analysis.

items.title: Hospitals paid up to ten times more than GPs to monitor adult ADHD patients, LMC claims
items.summary: Exclusive GP leaders in one area have claimed they have been offered ten times less than hospitals to deliver the same ADHD service.

items.title: Children as young as 13 seen by NHS for bladder damage caused by ketamine
items.summary: Children as young as 13 for bladder problems associated with ketamine use according to doctors who set up an NHS clinic to manage the problem.

items.title: Panel sides with Operose as ICB ‘breached regulations’ when awarding GP contracts
items.summary: An independent panel has sided with Operose as it found one ICB has breached regulations during contract awards for two London GP practices.

items.title: Can GPs win the fight for funding this time?
items.summary: Pulse editor Sofia Lind asks whether GPs can use the threat of industrial action to win greater control over their funding This week the BMA issued a stark warning about the NHS’s increasing reliance on non-doctors, with some seriously frightening examples of patient safety being put at risk.

items.title: Quick cases in gastroenterology
items.summary: Our latest CPD module explores five clinical scenarios in gastroenterology, covering ulcerative colitis flare, coeliac disease monitoring, persistent dyspepsia, chronic diarrhoea with a negative FIT result and interpreting liver scan findings. Complete the full module on Pulse 365 today.

items.title: Hospital signs lease for GP facilities in move towards providing neighbourhood services
items.summary: A hospital group said that it has ‘helped secure the future’ of a GP practice by signing a five-year lease agreement for its facilities, with a view to provide neighbourhood services in the future.

items.title: Current approach to detecting and treating hypertension is not working, say researchers
items.summary: The current approach to detecting and treating hypertension is ‘not fit for purpose’ say researchers who found high levels of undiagnosed and uncontrolled disease across the country.

items.title: More nurses needed in primary care to meet vaccination demand, conference hears
items.summary: Primary care services require more nurses to help meet expanding vaccination schedules and to ensure enough appointments are available, a Nursing in Practice conference has heard.

items.title: Minister reiterates nurse pay is up to GP practices to decide
items.summary: The new minister responsible for general practice has recognised that GP contractual arrangements ‘do not place any specific obligations’ on practices when it comes to nurse terms and conditions.

items.title: ‘As budgets get squished, so do school nursing teams’
items.summary: Professional officer and clinical school nurse lead Susie Scale has shared the diverse roles of school nurses – highlighting it as one of the very few roles to work between health, education and social care.

items.title: Patient safety alert issued to prevent avoidable harm from hoists
items.summary: Health and care organisations have been told to take a series of ‘urgent and practical steps’ to reduce avoidable harms when using patient hoists.

items.title: Practices struggling to stay open due to ‘severe’ nursing shortages
items.summary: GP practices in Wales are struggling to stay open amid a ‘severe shortage’ of nurses and other primary care colleagues, a new report has warned.

items.title: Polymyalgia rheumatica – when to suspect and how to test for it
items.summary: Under the radar: GPSI in MSK medicine Dr Louise Warburton describes how polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) symptoms can be misattributed – in this case to work stress and worsening osteoarthritis – and explains how symptoms and signs can be recognised and investigated promptly Note the case in this article is hypothetical…

items.title: GPs should let parents access children’s records but keep this ‘under review’, says GMC
items.summary: GPs should let parents access their child’s medical records if the child consents, but they should keep this decision ‘under review’, the GMC has said in new draft guidance.

items.title: General Practice Awards 2026 shortlist revealed
items.summary: The shortlist for the General Practice Awards 2026 has been revealed, with nurses and nursing teams among those being recognised for their contribution to patient care across the UK. More than 300 entries were received across 22 categories this year, celebrating achievements from across primary care.

items.title: Four in 10 GPs feel ‘unable to cope with stress’ at least weekly, RCGP warns
items.summary: Four in 10 GPs in Northern Ireland feel ‘unable to cope’ with stress every week, a new RCGP policy paper has found. The findings were presented at Stormont this week, as the college warned that the future sustainability of GP services is ‘at risk’ unless urgent action is taken now.

items.title: HPV self-testing kits: what nurses need to know
items.summary: Lead nurse at The Eve Appeal charity Helen Hyndman sets out what nurses need to know about the roll out of HPV self-testing kits and how the profession can play an important role in educating and supporting patients to participate in the cervical screening process.

items.title: Common cold vaccine shows promise in early trial
items.summary: A potential vaccine against the viruses responsible for most common colds has produced encouraging early results in its first human trial. The vaccine candidate, APL-10456, was developed through a collaboration between Imperial College London and biopharmaceutical firm Apollo Therapeutics.

items.title: GP practices denied premises upgrade funding due to legacy debt disputes
items.summary: Exclusive Debt disputes between GP practices and NHS Property Services (NHSPS) are blocking vital upgrades for additional clinical space, Pulse has learned.

items.title: Closure of 106 practices resulted in 31% more patients per GP, BMA finds
items.summary: The Welsh Government must increase the proportion to NHS budget spent in general practice to 11% in the next five years to prevent more practices from closing, the BMA has demanded.

items.title: Semaglutide linked to 40% reduction in asthma attacks
items.summary: Weight loss and diabetes treatment semaglutide is associated with a nearly 40% reduction in asthma attacks among people with the condition, according to new analysis.

items.title: Urine test could speed up bladder cancer diagnosis in patients with haematuria
items.summary: A non-invasive urine test could speed up diagnosis of bladder cancer, an NHS study has found. Trials of the GALEAS urine bladder test across seven NHS sites found it discovered nine in ten patients with the disease.

items.title: Womb cancer tests could be used in primary care
items.summary: A test to rule out womb cancer in women who experience bleeding after menopause could be used in primary care, a study has found. The University of Manchester study found that the test – which uses urine and vaginal fluid – correctly identified more than 80% of cancers and achieved a negative predictive value of...

items.title: GPC and RCGP go from balls-up to ballsy
items.summary: Copperfield is feeling positive for once, heaping some unexpected praise on the suddenly braver-sounding BMA and RCGP It can be a lonely place, general practice. Especially mid-Monday morning, running late, with tasks, labs and letters already overflowing.

items.title: BMA calls for ‘urgent review’ of advanced practitioner scopes over patient safety concerns
items.summary: The British Medical Association (BMA) is calling for an ‘urgent review’ of advanced practitioners’ (APs) scopes of practice after publishing doctors’ accounts alleging patient safety risks.

items.title: Government urged to establish ‘primary care access standard’
items.summary: The Government should establish a ‘primary care access standard’ and extend GP access measurement to populations currently missing from NHS data, a think tank and an all-party parliamentary group have recommended.

items.title: BMA report reveals accounts of non-doctors rejecting GP referrals and ‘taking the role of GPs’
items.summary: The BMA is calling for an end to the ‘taskification’ of medicine – the shifting of more and more tasks to non-doctor professions – after it received accounts of non-doctors rejecting GP referrals and ‘taking the role of GPs’.

items.title: Genetic changes causing severe Kent MenB outbreak, scientists confirm
items.summary: Scientists say they have pinpointed the genetic changes that made the deadly meningitis B (MenB) outbreak in Kent earlier this year so severe.

items.title: Interview: RCN director sets out GPN pay ‘movement’ and next steps
items.summary: In an exclusive interview with Nursing in Practice, Royal College of Nursing (RCN) executive director for England Patricia Marquis reflects on recent efforts to improve general practice nurse (GPN) pay and conditions and sets out the college’s next steps for supporting the workforce.

items.title: Advanced practice nurses are ‘a global health priority’, says ICN chief executive
items.summary: The chief executive of the International Council of Nurses (ICN) has described advanced practice nursing as ‘critical’ to strengthening prevention and primary care and called on further political investment to ‘turn it from a missed opportunity into a global health priority.’ Speaking at the annual Advanced Practice…

items.title: BMA warns practices against piloting ‘GP in your pocket’ AI tool
items.summary: The BMA has warned GP practices against getting involved in pilots of AI-assisted triage within the NHS App. The union said that expressions of interest have been going out to practices and PCNs to pilot AI technology which was announced in the 10-year health plan.

items.title: ‘A little advice and guidance for our hospital colleagues’
items.summary: Enthused by the ‘roaring’ success of advice and guidance for GPs, Dr Toni Munno proposes setting up a parallel system for secondary care colleagues I personally think the advice and guidance service is working so well that I’d like to set one up for hospital doctors.

items.title: Life-extending breast cancer drug approved for NHS following price deal
items.summary: NICE has finally recommended the life-extending breast cancer drug Enhertu for routine NHS use after reaching a new commercial arrangement.

items.title: Too many QOF targets ‘blur and fragment’ GP priorities, NHS productivity commission warns
items.summary: The health service is struggling because it has ‘too many targets’ and ‘not enough focus on outcomes’, the NHS productivity commission has found.

items.title: NICE backs endometriosis saliva test for use in primary care
items.summary: A non-invasive saliva test to help diagnose endometriosis earlier is being recommended for use in primary care, under updated draft guidance from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE).

items.title: General Practice Awards 2026 shortlist revealed
items.summary: The shortlist for the General Practice Awards 2026 has been revealed, recognising some of the individuals and teams making a difference to patients and primary care across the UK. This year, more than 300 entries were submitted across 22 awards, celebrating achievement throughout primary care.

items.title: Workforce planning ‘limited’ as general practice nurses omitted from vacancy data, says RCN
items.summary: Efforts to improve workforce planning for nurses are ‘limited’ due to the vacancy rates amongst general practice nurses (GPNs) being omitted from published data, a Royal College of Nursing (RCN) report has highlighted.

items.title: NMC to develop principles for ‘safe and responsible’ AI use with other regulators
items.summary: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) is to help develop shared principles on artificial intelligence (AI) to ensure ‘safe and responsible’ use by healthcare professionals in the UK.

items.title: Willingness to seek help may explain rising mental health demand among young people
items.summary: An increase in demand for GP appointments for mental health issues may be down to a greater willingness among young people to seek help, a study has found. Norwegian researchers said mental health problems have being reported to have risen in many high-income countries, particularly among teens and young adults.

items.title: ‘In the beginning there was love’
items.summary: Placing third in our writing competition, Dr Paul McNamara recalls how his mother’s addiction and death by suicide have impacted how he understands patients and suffering as a GP In the beginning there was love. When the boy was 15, the tiny house slowly filled with booze and fags and shut out the light.

items.title: £50 extra per patient to be ‘major negotiating aim’ in GP contract talks, says BMA
items.summary: Securing additional GP core funding equivalent to £50 per patient is a ‘major negotiating aim’ in the BMA’s current talks with the Government, the union has revealed.

items.title: Whistleblowing reports to the NMC increase by almost 7%
items.summary: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) received 159 ‘qualifying’ whistleblowing disclosures during the most recent financial year, an increase of almost 7%.

items.title: Nurses asked for views in ‘NHS-wide conversation’ on maternity and neonatal services
items.summary: An NHS survey asking nurses to share their views and help shape improvements to maternity and neonatal services as part of an ‘NHS-wide conversation’ has opened today.

items.title: Concerns raised as data reveals ‘dramatic and significant’ decline in health visitors and school nurses across England
items.summary: Concerns have been raised by community nursing associations as new data has revealed a ‘dramatic and significant’ decline in the number of health visitors and school nurses across England.

items.title: GPs to ‘limit appointments’ if Government doesn’t engage in contract talks
items.summary: Exclusive The BMA has drawn up plans to escalate GP collective action if ‘insufficient progress’ is made in discussions with the Government, Pulse has learnt.

items.title: Dementia care needs same ambition as cancer, argues report
items.summary: Dementia needs the same investment that has transformed cancer survival in recent decades if any real progress is to be made, a report has concluded. The King’s Fund and Alzheimer’s Society said dementia care is stuck in the 20th century and needs a ‘cancer-style revolution’.

items.title: Tailored falls prevention programmes no better than offering advice and exercise
items.summary: Personalised programmes to prevent falls in older people may make no difference, according to a comprehensive review of the evidence.

items.title: Anaphylaxis: myths and facts explained
items.summary: GP with an interest in allergy Dr Elizabeth Angier dispels some common myths and highlights some under-recognised facts regarding anaphylaxis MYTHS Myth 1.

items.title: Declines in syphilis and gonorrhoea diagnoses in England, data reveals
items.summary: The number of syphilis and gonorrhoea diagnoses among gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) has declined, new data has revealed.

items.title: Nurse makes history in Wales as first independent care home nurse prescriber
items.summary: A care home nurse has become the first in Wales to qualify to prescribe medication to residents. Ezelina Dacruz qualified from Bangor University while working as a clinical lead at Glan Rhos Nursing Home in Anglesey, where she has worked for more than 20 years.

items.title: GP practices should stop using sessions as units of time to ensure safe working
items.summary: The BMA in Scotland has recommended practices move away from using sessions as the basic units of GP time, to help ensure safe working.

items.title: Majority of GPs think ADHD is ‘overdiagnosed’, suggests Pulse survey
items.summary: Exclusive Seven in 10 GPs think adult ADHD is ‘overdiagnosed’, including nearly half who think it is ‘very overdiagnosed’, a Pulse survey has suggested. More than eight in 10 patients referred to adult ADHD services receive a positive diagnosis, GPs in the survey also estimated.

items.title: Nurses report an ‘increase in deaths and maggots in wounds’ amid summer heatwave
items.summary: Nurses report an ‘increase in deaths’ during the summer heatwave, finding maggots in wounds and cancer patients ‘dripping with sweat’, a survey has revealed.

items.title: The best of Pulse’s 2026 GP writing competition
items.summary: Earlier this year we put out a call to all Pulse readers to find our next GP blogger and were subsequently inundated with more than 100 entries – the most we have ever had for a writing competition.

items.title: ‘Alarming’ rise in children attending A&E in mental health crisis
items.summary: A growing number of children and young people ending up in A&E with mental health concerns because of a lack of alternative options is a ‘national crisis’, the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH) has warned.

items.title: Many GPs cannot access key asthma test for children
items.summary: GPs across large parts of the country cannot access a key, NICE-recommended test for diagnosing asthma in children, a charity has warned.

items.title: Nurses asked to consult on guidance aimed at improving diagnosis of OCD and BDD
items.summary: Nurses and other healthcare professionals are being asked to consult on draft guidance which aims to improve the identification of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and body dysmorphic disorder (BDD).

items.title: BMA postpones GP collective action escalation as it re-enters ‘bilateral’ contract talks
items.summary: The BMA’s GP committee has decided to postpone collective action escalation until 1 December, in a bid to ‘reset’ relationships, as GPC re-enters ‘bilateral talks’ with the Government and NHS England.

items.title: Autumn Budget must ring-fence GP funding for 10-year plan, says RCGP
items.summary: The RCGP has urged the Treasury to ring-fence funding specifically for GP recruitment and retention, if it wants to meet the ambitions set out in the 10-year plan.
